data.comments:
(en)

In Andorra, transhumance is primarily vertical: in spring and summer, herds of cattle, horses, and sheep move up to graze in high-mountain pastures, while in autumn, they descend to lower-lying areas to escape the winter. Since December 2023, it has been recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

Characteristics and traditions

• Vertical transhumance: Livestock move between the valleys and the peaks of the Pyrenees (such as the Incles Valley).

• UNESCO Heritage: Andorra is part of an international nomination led by Spain, alongside other European countries.

• Cultural events: Notable local celebrations include the “Benedicció de Setúria” in La Massana, which features symbolic processions of livestock through town centers, as well as various community activities.

• Hiking routes: There are tourist and cross-border trails, such as the path between the Plateau de Beille (Ariège, France) and the Incles Valley, that follow ancient pastoral routes.
